  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 369,
      "endEvent": 375,
      "contextStartEvent": 309,
      "contextEndEvent": 393,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "it will never be rational to accept moral skepticism",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Craig endorses Anthony's categorical ranking of every skeptical argument below moral experience (E369–375), preemptively neutralizing counterarguments without examining their premises. This is an explicit epistemic protection within an argument, not an unsupported slogan: E365–368 supplies moral experience as the reason, although nothing establishes the unrestricted ranking of all possible objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 790,
      "endEvent": 799,
      "contextStartEvent": 782,
      "contextEndEvent": 817,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "should result in the Physicians being struck off for incompetence",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Atkins treats physicians' certification of a cure as lacking a natural explanation as grounds for professional disqualification (E790–799), without examining any case. This protects his universal denial by discrediting contrary assessors. His narrower objection to inferring divine intervention from unexplained recovery is legitimate in principle, but that distinction is not developed here."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 879,
      "endEvent": 886,
      "contextStartEvent": 834,
      "contextEndEvent": 893,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "there is no longer any need to think",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort",
        "shame",
        "identity",
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The closing choice makes accepting God equivalent to abandoning thought, replacing a missing reason why theistic belief excludes continued inquiry. Earlier arguments address explanatory alternatives (E632–864), not that incompatibility. The explicit reference to accepting God 'on faith alone' (E879–880) narrows the target, making a general protection against reasoned theistic objections uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1234,
      "endEvent": 1235,
      "contextStartEvent": 1201,
      "contextEndEvent": 1235,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "never listen to an argument about Infinity it's infinitely slippery",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The injunction substitutes a blanket dismissal for showing why arguments concerning infinity should never receive consideration, and expressly excludes that class of objections. Atkins does offer Zeno's successive divisions and a distinction between solar-system age and cosmic history (E1209–1233); those reasons address particular arguments but do not earn the unrestricted prohibition."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1356,
      "endEvent": 1359,
      "contextStartEvent": 1354,
      "contextEndEvent": 1393,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "there's always more reason to believe to disbelieve the report than there is to believe what is reported",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Atkins endorses an apparently exceptionless maxim against miracle reports (E1356–1359), potentially deciding against testimony regardless of its strength. However, he subsequently supplies source-reliability objections and asks for extraordinary evidence (E1360–1389). Those qualifications leave uncertain whether the maxim replaces assessment or states a defeasible evidential judgment about these reports."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1615,
      "endEvent": 1621,
      "contextStartEvent": 1543,
      "contextEndEvent": 1719,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "there is no evidence whatsoever for any assertion that Dr Craig has made this evening",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The universal dismissal replaces an account of why every offered premise lacks evidence, extending beyond Atkins's specific criticisms of causality and historical testimony. Craig has explicitly offered scientific and historical support (E1453–1475, E1543–1606). Atkins does supply substantive objections elsewhere, but the claim that everything is accepted on faith exceeds those objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1810,
      "endEvent": 1814,
      "contextStartEvent": 1802,
      "contextEndEvent": 1818,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "any argument for moral skepticism will be based upon premises which are less obviously true",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "After intervening replies, Craig renews the universal priority assigned to moral conviction over skeptical premises (E1810–1814). That priority preemptively discounts every counterargument. It remains a philosophical argument rather than a slogan: moral experience was supplied as support (E1530–1535), but the claim that all possible skeptical premises are less evident remains unearned."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1962,
      "endEvent": 1969,
      "contextStartEvent": 1883,
      "contextEndEvent": 1981,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "they are the ears that are determined not to revise their prejudices",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "ridicule",
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Atkins explains present receptiveness to Craig by fixed prejudice and intellectual laziness (E1962–1969), making disagreement evidence of audience defects rather than assessing its reasons. Earlier criticisms of logic, causality, and testimony provide substantive context (E1887–1921), but do not establish this unrestricted diagnosis. The passage is a protected dismissal, not clearly a repeatable slogan."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 982,
      "endEvent": 990,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "as long as that is even possibly true it shows that God and Evil are logically consistent",
      "explanation": "Craig explicitly limits the sufficient-reasons hypothesis to demonstrating logical compatibility. This does not itself explain actual suffering or defeat an evidential argument, but a possible counterexample is relevant to strict contradiction. E955–974 shows that he has framed the target that narrowly."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 655,
      "endEvent": 664,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "when there is absolutely nothing there are no physical laws no Quantum fluctuation",
      "explanation": "Atkins distinguishes a daughter universe arising within an existing physical framework from an original universe. He explains why quantum-vacuum language cannot automatically answer the latter question, and expressly acknowledges the absence of a known account at E632–642 and E712–715."
    }
